string.text: Callback monitoring, performance profiling, and testing.
Count and log every callback this game version defines.
Also watch the callbacks that fire every frame or every shot, such as NPC shots, bullet hits and combat distance checks. They flood the log in a firefight.
Log top-firing callbacks at regular intervals.
[seconds]\nHow often to log periodic statistics. Range 10-3600.
Log callback arguments/parameters. Can create large log files.
Extract detailed info from objects (type, name, section, community).
Maximum depth for table introspection (1-4). Higher = more detail but larger logs.
Scan smart terrain distances, stash density, base spacing, and feature distribution per level. Fires on level load and periodically. Log output: logs/testzone.log

For when every timer in the game stops at once: HUDs never appear, stat panels freeze, and nothing is logged. Records whether the timer queue registered at load and which timer broke it. After a freeze, run_string tz_watcher.log_queue_state() names the timer left mid-call. Takes effect on the next game load. Log output: logs/testzone.log
Limit log frequency per callback type. Prevents log spam from high-frequency callbacks.
[milliseconds]\nMinimum time between logs for same callback type. Range 100-10000.
Opens the AnimationTool on the stalker you look at. Esc closes it.
Periodic scan of all mutant squads. Logs species, faction, online/offline, smart terrain, commander fields.
[seconds]\nHow often the mutant scan runs. Range 5-300.
Periodic scan of the current level: squads, smart terrains, stashes, and the AP squad overlay.
[seconds]\nHow often the level scan runs. Range 10-300.
World-wide squad census: totals by faction, by level, and online/offline counts.
[seconds]\nHow often the world scan runs. Range 30-600.
Watcher logs all 162 engine callbacks. Log output: logs/testzone.log
Wraps suspect GAMMA mod functions with timing to measure actual frame cost.
Start recording timing data for wrapped functions. Functions are always wrapped, this controls measurement.
[seconds]\nHow often to log profiler report. Range 10-300.
[microseconds]\nSingle call exceeding this value counts as a spike. Range 100-10000.
Profiler wraps 22 suspect functions identified from GAMMA review. Log output: logs/testzone.log
What the stalkers and mutants near you hear, see, remember, take as danger and pick as enemy. One line per change. Output: logs/testzone_perception.log
Every hearing event that reaches him, with its power against his threshold. One line per source and sound type per half second.
When he starts or stops seeing you, and his detection progress in 10 percent steps.
His visual, sound and hit memory of you: presence, age and payload, on every change. Mutants: visual only.
His held danger with the action answering it down to the leaf (take cover, look out, hold, detour, search), and his reaction with the distance he moved. Stalkers only.
Who he picks as enemy and drops, and whether this log saw him hear or see you before the pick.
Subjects within this distance of you are tracked (meters).
Hearing events from every source, not only yours. One line per subject and source per second at most.
Track mutants as well as stalkers. Every line carries the kind.
Reads engine state only. Works the same with any AI mod on or off, so two runs compare. Log output: logs/testzone_perception.log
GeoTool shows every place check live at your spot and saves notes with the position and the readings to its file in the logs folder.
Opens the GeoTool window. Esc closes it.
[seconds] How often the open window reads every check.
Notes go to one file per game run in the logs folder, geo_tool and the launch time, one tab-separated line each.
SoundTool plays channels, DiegeticDread categories, NPC voice and any .ogg on disk, and writes your notes to its file in the logs folder.
Opens the SoundTool window. Esc closes it.

Silences the soundscape, weapons and music, and SoundTool's own plays still sound. A sound already playing runs to its end, so turn it on, then save and load: after the load nothing starts. Steps, NPC voices, mutants and crows keep playing.
Files from outside the game are copied into sounds/sound_tool_cache while the window is open and deleted when it closes.
Every sound the soundscape plays, with its channel, distance, map and weather. On a modded exe with the mix meter, also how loud the mix is. Output: logs/testzone_sound_trace.log
Logs every sound the soundscape plays, with its channel, distance, map and weather, to logs/testzone_sound_trace.log.
The sound trace also logs script sounds outside the ambient channels, such as music, the interface and DiegeticDread's cues.
A run on plain Anomaly, GAMMA or the Diegetic mods compares line for line. Log output: logs/testzone_sound_trace.log

Runs Lua files dropped into appdata/testzone from outside the game. A file in inbox runs once and is removed, and a file in watch runs on every load and again whenever it changes. Each run writes its result to outbox, and a failed run also leaves its file in error. Works only when the game starts with -dbg.
Checks the inbox and watch folders once a second while a level runs. Any program on this computer can then run code in the game, so leave it off when you are not testing.
stalker-manager testzone-send drops a file and prints its result. Log output: logs/testzone_remote.log
Logging level and flush for every TestZone subsystem. Output: logs/testzone.log
Minimum severity written to the log. DEBUG shows everything, ERROR almost nothing.
Write each line to disk at once instead of buffering. Slower, but the log stays current while you tail it.
Restore all TestZone MCM settings to defaults. Use after upgrading from a version with a different MCM structure.
Warning: save or discard pending MCM changes first, otherwise they override the reset on the next Apply.
TestZone: all settings restored to defaults.

GeoTool shows every place check at your spot, live while the window is open.
When a check reads your spot wrong, write a note, and the note keeps the spot with every reading.
 
%c[255,200,170,120]The position
%c[default]The top screen shows the level, the level vertex and your position as X, Y and Z in whole metres.
 
%c[255,200,170,120]The readings
%c[default]While the green lamp is lit, the middle screen refreshes the readings.
%c[255,235,240,245]smart%c[default] is the nearest smart terrain, its distance, and whether it is a base or a lair.
%c[255,235,240,245]base_owner%c[default] is the nearest trader, medic or mechanic within 80 metres.
%c[255,235,240,245]is_indoor%c[default] is the xlibs test, a roof within 4 metres and two walls within 5.
%c[255,235,240,245]roof%c[default] is the roof alone, from a ray up, or from a ray down when the upward ray misses.
%c[255,235,240,245]roof_walls%c[default] is the raw roof distance and wall count behind is_indoor.
%c[255,235,240,245]underground%c[default] tells whether the level counts as underground.
%c[255,235,240,245]surge_cover%c[default] tells whether the emission treats your spot as cover.
%c[255,235,240,245]safe_cover%c[default] tells whether the game flags you as sheltered.
%c[255,235,240,245]rain%c[default] is how much rain reaches you.
%c[255,235,240,245]sky%c[default] is how much open sky lights you, and under 0.05 the game counts you as indoor.
 
%c[255,200,170,120]Notes
%c[default]Type a note and press the plus key.
The line keeps the time, the level, your position, the vertex and every reading.
An empty note saves the spot alone, and the bottom screen shows your last two notes.
Your notes go to geo_tool with the launch time, in the logs folder.
 
%c[255,200,170,120]Keys
%c[default]%c[255,235,240,245]Del%c[default] opens the window and %c[255,235,240,245]Esc%c[default] closes it.
MCM sets the open key and how often the readings refresh.

AnimationTool plays a motion or a state on a stalker, and you judge each one good or bad.
Your calls go to its file in the logs folder, one file per game run.
 
%c[255,200,170,120]The stalker
%c[default]Look at a stalker and open the tool, and he stays bound while the window is open.
His name shows on the screen, then the state last asked of him.
After the arrow comes the animation he plays now.
%c[255,235,240,245]select%c[default] keeps the stalker you aim at, or the bound one, bound each time you open the tool.
%c[255,235,240,245]reset%c[default] drops him, and the screen shows NO NPC until you open the tool again.
 
%c[255,200,170,120]The list
%c[default]%c[255,235,240,245]browse files%c[default] opens the logs folder. Two dots go up a folder, and above a drive you see every drive.
Every .tsv or .txt file in configs/testzone/anim follows, and a click on a file lists its motions.
 
%c[255,200,170,120]Playback
%c[default]%c[255,235,240,245]play%c[default] or a double click plays the motion on him, and %c[255,235,240,245]stop%c[default] sends him back to idle.
%c[255,235,240,245]prev%c[default] and %c[255,235,240,245]next%c[default] step to the neighbouring motion and play it.
%c[255,235,240,245]pose%c[default] plays the motion standing in place, and %c[255,235,240,245]moving%c[default] plays it while he walks.
A click on either key replays the motion at once.
States from the dig list play the way the game wires them and ignore pose and moving.
The prop row at the top of a playlist attaches an item, like a bottle, a guitar or a knife.
Your pick replays the motion with the item, and it stays until you pick none.
While a motion holds on him the green lamp stays lit, and the red lamp lights when it stops.
A motion plays only when his animation file is loaded, and an unknown name plays nothing.
 
%c[255,200,170,120]Notes
%c[default]%c[255,235,240,245]good%c[default] and %c[255,235,240,245]bad%c[default] write the motion with that call and the typed note.
The plus key writes the typed note with the call note.
Each line also keeps the playlist and the posture.
Your last two lines show on the bottom screen.
 
%c[255,200,170,120]Keys
%c[default]%c[255,235,240,245]PgDn%c[default] opens the window, %c[255,235,240,245]Esc%c[default] closes it and sends the stalker back to idle, and MCM sets the open key.

SoundTool plays any sound the way the game plays it, at your ear, at a distance you pick.
Your notes go to a file in the logs folder, a new file each time you start the game.
 
%c[255,200,170,120]The list
%c[default]%c[255,235,240,245]browse files%c[default] opens the logs folder. Two dots go up a folder, and above a drive you see all drives.
If you have DiegeticDread, the dread categories come next.
All channels that play a file follow, each with the distance where the game plays it.
If a folder holds .ogg files, %c[255,235,240,245]play this folder%c[default] lists them. A .txt file opens as a playlist.
The loop key at the top reads all these lists again, for example after you add a file.
 
%c[255,200,170,120]Playlists
%c[default]Each entry of a playlist names a sound by its game path, like zs/spook/raven_1.
You can also give an absolute path, and even a path next to the playlist works.
Put %c[255,235,240,245]base:%c[default] and a folder in a comment, and the next relative paths start in that folder.
Your comment right above a sound shows on the screen with that sound.
An entry that names neither a file nor a folder is a divider.
We copy each outside file into sounds/sound_tool_cache, since the game plays only indexed files.
 
%c[255,200,170,120]Playback
%c[default]Click a sound to play it, and use the previous and next keys to move without playing.
%c[255,235,240,245]stop%c[default] ends only the sounds this tool started.
%c[255,235,240,245]game%c[default] plays the sound the way the game code does, with a new random roll for each click.
For an outside file, and for game code we do not replay yet, %c[255,235,240,245]game%c[default] is off.
%c[255,235,240,245]2D%c[default] plays the sound at your ear. %c[255,235,240,245]3D%c[default] plays the sound in front of you, at the distance in the box.
A distance key plays the sound at that distance, while %c[255,235,240,245]height%c[default] lifts the 3D play.
If both %c[255,235,240,245]falloff%c[default] boxes hold a min and a larger max, the file will play with that falloff.
Your volume keys set how loud the next play is, from 0.1 to 1.0.
The green lamp stays lit while a sound plays, but the red lamp lights once all of them have ended.
 
%c[255,200,170,120]The screen
%c[default]The first row names the game code that plays the file, or where an outside file would play.
Below it you see the distance, the height and the volume of the last play.
The third row shows the measured loudness, with an estimate at the spot of the last play.
For an outside file you see its playlist note instead, followed by the falloff stored in the file.
 
%c[255,200,170,120]Notes
%c[default]Type a note, keep, reject and whatever more you need, then press the plus key.
Each note keeps the sound, the game code and the last roll.
Your last two notes show on the bottom screen.
 
%c[255,200,170,120]Quiet audition
%c[default]If you need silence to judge a sound, turn on %c[255,235,240,245]Mute%c[default] in the MCM SoundTool tab, then save and load.
The soundscape, the weapons and the music will stay silent, but this tool still plays.
Steps, NPC voices, mutants and crows keep playing, because our hooks do not reach them.
While the window is open, DiegeticDread stays silent even with Mute off.
 
%c[255,200,170,120]Keys
%c[default]%c[255,235,240,245]End%c[default] opens the window and %c[255,235,240,245]Esc%c[default] closes it, and you can change the open key in MCM.
